records.context: A spaCR project is a folder of derived data.  ``merged/`` came from raw images, ``measurements.db`` came from ``merged/``, the model came from the extracted image regions the database indexes, and the hit list came from the model.  The files themselves do not record these links, so without a registry a result cannot be checked against its inputs: after Mask is executed again with a different diameter, every downstream number is out of date and nothing marks it.
records.label: spacr.artifacts#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A spaCR project is a folder of derived data.  ``merged/`` came from raw images, ``measurements.db`` came from ``merged/``, the model came from the crops the database indexes, and the hit list came from the model.  The files themselves do not record these links, so without a registry a result cannot be checked against its inputs: after Mask is re-run with a different diameter, every downstream number is out of date and nothing marks it.
records.translation: Ett spaCR-projekt är en mapp med härledda data.  ``merged/`` kom från råbilder, ``measurements.db`` kom från ``merged/``, modellen kom från de utklipp som databasen indexerar, och träfflistan kom från modellen.  Filerna själva registrerar inte dessa kopplingar, så utan ett register kan ett resultat inte kontrolleras mot sina indata: efter att Mask har körts om med en annan diameter är varje efterföljande tal inaktuellt och inget markerar det.

records.context: Storage is SQLite — ``artifacts.db`` in the project root, one row per artifact plus one edge row per input — because two Measure workers, a GUI and a batch runner can all be touching a project at once, and a pickle cannot survive that.  Writes go through :func:`spacr.database_concurrency.transaction` with an explicit lock budget, which is also why nothing here does its own retry arithmetic.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Storage is SQLite — ``artifacts.db`` in the project root, one row per artifact plus one edge row per input — because two Measure workers, a GUI and a batch runner can all be touching a project at once, and a pickle cannot survive that.  Writes go through :func:`spacr.database_concurrency.transaction` with an explicit lock budget, which is also why nothing here does its own retry arithmetic.
records.translation: Lagringen är SQLite — ``artifacts.db`` i projektroten, en rad per artefakt plus en kantrad per indata — eftersom två Measure-arbetare, ett GUI och en batchkörare alla kan röra ett projekt samtidigt, och en pickle klarar inte det.  Skrivningar går via :func:`spacr.database_concurrency.transaction` med en uttrycklig låsbudget, vilket också är varför inget här utför sin egen omförsöksaritmetik.

records.context: A regular file is hashed end to end while it is small enough to be worth it, and above ``full_hash_limit`` from its size plus its first and last megabyte — enough to notice a rewritten database without spending minutes of I/O at the end of every processing session. A folder is fingerprinted from its file inventory: each file's relative path, size and modification time, in sorted order. Symlinks are skipped — linked files are ignored and linked subfolders are not descended into — so a folder of links fingerprints as empty.
records.label: spacr.artifacts.content_fingerprint#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A regular file is hashed end to end while it is small enough to be worth it, and above ``full_hash_limit`` from its size plus its first and last megabyte — enough to notice a rewritten database without spending minutes of I/O at the end of every run. A folder is fingerprinted from its file inventory: each file's relative path, size and modification time, in sorted order. Symlinks are skipped — linked files are ignored and linked subfolders are not descended into — so a folder of links fingerprints as empty.
records.translation: En vanlig fil hashas från början till slut så länge den är liten nog för att det ska löna sig, och över ``full_hash_limit`` utifrån sin storlek plus sin första och sista megabyte — tillräckligt för att upptäcka en omskriven databas utan att lägga minuter av I/O i slutet av varje körning. En mapp får sitt fingeravtryck från sin filförteckning: varje fils relativa sökväg, storlek och ändringstid, i sorterad ordning. Symboliska länkar hoppas över — länkade filer ignoreras och länkade undermappar gås inte in i — så att en mapp med länkar får fingeravtrycket för en tom mapp.

records.context: This module is the other axis. It holds a software job list of arbitrary ``(module, settings)`` jobs in any order: ``Mask → Measure → Classify (CV) → Classify (ML)``, then the same four again with a different diameter, then a fifth plate's Mask.

records.source: This module is the other axis. It holds a queue of arbitrary ``(module, settings)`` jobs in any order: ``Mask → Measure → Classify (CV) → Classify (ML)``, then the same four again with a different diameter, then a fifth plate's Mask.
records.translation: Denna modul är den andra axeln. Den innehåller en kö med godtyckliga ``(module, settings)``-jobb i valfri ordning: ``Mask → Measure → Classify (CV) → Classify (ML)``, sedan samma fyra igen med en annan diameter, sedan en femte plattas Mask.

records.context: A queued job **is** a ``spacr-run`` invocation. Nothing here re-implements module dispatch or settings loading: :mod:`spacr.cli` owns the module registry, the settings loader, the ``--set`` coercion and the exit-code contract (0 ok, 1 the module raised, 2 bad arguments or settings), and this module drives it. The software job list's own result is a :class:`spacr.errors.RunLedger`, stamped next to the software job list file, and each job's :func:`spacr.errors.read_run_status` stamp is read back so a job that exited 0 having silently skipped 40 fields is reported as *partial* rather than as a success.
records.label: spacr.batch#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A queued job **is** a ``spacr-run`` invocation. Nothing here re-implements module dispatch or settings loading: :mod:`spacr.cli` owns the module registry, the settings loader, the ``--set`` coercion and the exit-code contract (0 ok, 1 the module raised, 2 bad arguments or settings), and this module drives it. The queue's own result is a :class:`spacr.errors.RunLedger`, stamped next to the queue file, and each job's :func:`spacr.errors.read_run_status` stamp is read back so a job that exited 0 having silently skipped 40 fields is reported as *partial* rather than as a success.
records.translation: Ett köat jobb **är** ett anrop av ``spacr-run``. Inget här implementerar modulutskick eller inläsning av inställningar på nytt: :mod:`spacr.cli` äger modulregistret, inställningsinläsaren, omvandlingen för ``--set`` och kontraktet för avslutningskoder (0 ok, 1 modulen utlöste ett undantag, 2 felaktiga argument eller inställningar), och denna modul styr det. Köns eget resultat är en :class:`spacr.errors.RunLedger`, stämplad bredvid köfilen, och varje jobbs stämpel från :func:`spacr.errors.read_run_status` läses tillbaka så att ett jobb som avslutades med 0 efter att tyst ha hoppat över 40 bildfält rapporteras som *partiellt* i stället för som lyckat.

records.source: Behaviour for unattended runs:
records.translation: Beteende för obevakade körningar:

records.context: **Every job is validated when it is added, not when it executes.** :func:`validate_queue` reports *all* problems at once and :func:`run_queue` refuses to start while any of them is an error.
records.label: spacr.batch#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Every job is validated when it is added, not when it runs.** :func:`validate_queue` reports *all* problems at once and :func:`run_queue` refuses to start while any of them is an error.
records.translation: **Varje jobb valideras när det läggs till, inte när det körs.** :func:`validate_queue` rapporterar *alla* problem på en gång och :func:`run_queue` vägrar starta så länge något av dem är ett fel.

records.context: **State is persisted after every transition, atomically.** A machine that reboots while processing the software job list is resumed with :func:`resume_queue`, not restarted. The file is written to a temp name and ``os.replace``\ d, so a crash cannot leave a truncated work list file.
records.label: spacr.batch#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **State is persisted after every transition, atomically.** A machine that reboots mid-queue is resumed with :func:`resume_queue`, not restarted. The file is written to a temp name and ``os.replace``\ d, so a crash cannot leave a truncated queue file.
records.translation: **Tillståndet sparas efter varje övergång, atomärt.** En maskin som startar om mitt i kön återupptas med :func:`resume_queue`, den startas inte om från början. Filen skrivs till ett temporärt namn och flyttas på plats med ``os.replace``, så att en krasch inte kan lämna en trunkerad köfil.

records.context: **A job whose dependency failed is skipped, not executed.** Measure after a failed Mask produces a database that looks like a real result. ``skipped`` (deliberately not executed), ``failed`` and ``not_run`` (the software job list halted before reaching it) are three different things and stay that way.
records.label: spacr.batch#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

records.context: Jobs that already succeeded are left alone. Jobs that were ``not_run`` (the software job list halted before reaching them) or still ``pending`` are executed. A job that was ``running`` when the machine went down is reset and run again. For Mask, Measure, and Format Converter jobs the rerun receives ``resume=True`` automatically, so their verified microscope field of view checkpoints are reused instead of repeating the whole laboratory microplate. Failed and skipped jobs stay as they are unless ``retry_failed`` is set.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Jobs that already succeeded are left alone. Jobs that were ``not_run`` (the queue halted before reaching them) or still ``pending`` are run. A job that was ``running`` when the machine went down is reset and run again. For Mask, Measure, and Format Converter jobs the rerun receives ``resume=True`` automatically, so their verified field checkpoints are reused instead of repeating the whole plate. Failed and skipped jobs stay as they are unless ``retry_failed`` is set.

records.context: The outer ring of a microtitre laboratory microplate evaporates faster, sits at a different temperature and is handled differently from the interior. A microplate sample position in row A or column 24 that reads three sigma from the laboratory microplate mean is therefore much more likely to be an artefact of *where it sits* than of what is in it.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The outer ring of a microtitre plate evaporates faster, sits at a different temperature and is handled differently from the interior. A well in row A or column 24 that reads three sigma from the plate mean is therefore much more likely to be an artefact of *where it sits* than of what is in it.
records.translation: Den yttre ringen på en mikrotiterplatta avdunstar snabbare, har en annan temperatur och hanteras annorlunda än det inre. En brunn i rad A eller kolumn 24 som ligger tre sigma från plattans medelvärde är därför mycket mer sannolikt en artefakt av *var den sitter* än av vad den innehåller.

records.context: **The laboratory microplate format is inferred, never assumed.** 6/12/24/48/96/384/1536 are recognised from the observed row and column labels, and the ring geometry uses the *nominal* grid of the inferred format. A screen that only used rows A-H of a 384 laboratory microplate does not get row H promoted to "edge" just because nothing was pipetted below it.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The plate format is inferred, never assumed.** 6/12/24/48/96/384/1536 are recognised from the observed row and column labels, and the ring geometry uses the *nominal* grid of the inferred format. records.context: **Rank tests, not t-tests.** Per-microplate sample position aggregates of object measurements are routinely skewed and heavy-tailed — a microplate sample position with three enormous cells is not a normal deviate. The ring comparison is a two-sided Mann-Whitney U; the gradient test is Spearman. Neither assumes a shape.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Rank tests, not t-tests.** Per-well aggregates of object measurements are routinely skewed and heavy-tailed — a well with three enormous cells is not a normal deviate. The ring comparison is a two-sided Mann-Whitney U; the gradient test is Spearman. Neither assumes a shape.
records.translation: **Rangtester, inte t-tester.** Aggregat per brunn av objektmätningar är rutinmässigt skeva och har tunga svansar — en brunn med tre enorma celler är ingen normalfördelad avvikelse. Ringjämförelsen är ett tvåsidigt Mann-Whitney U; gradienttestet är Spearman. Inget av dem antar en form.

records.context: **Effect size leads, p-value follows.** With 384 microplate sample positions, almost any systematic drift clears p < 0.05; that fact carries no information. Every comparison therefore reports the median difference, the difference as a percentage of the interior median, *and* Cliff's delta — a rank-based standardised effect in [-1, 1] read straight off the same U statistic (``δ = 2U/n₁n₂ − 1``). Detection requires both a small p **and** an effect size above :data:`DEFAULT_MIN_EFFECT`, so a significant but 0.4 % difference is not reported as an edge effect.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Effect size leads, p-value follows.** With 384 wells, almost any systematic drift clears p < 0.05; that fact carries no information. Every comparison therefore reports the median difference, the difference as a percentage of the interior median, *and* Cliff's delta — a rank-based standardised effect in [-1, 1] read straight off the same U statistic (``δ = 2U/n₁n₂ − 1``). Detection requires both a small p **and** an effect size above :data:`DEFAULT_MIN_EFFECT`, so a significant but 0.4 % difference is not reported as an edge effect.
records.translation: **Effektstorleken kommer först, p-värdet följer.** Med 384 brunnar klarar nästan varje systematisk förskjutning p < 0.05; det faktumet bär ingen information. Varje jämförelse rapporterar därför mediandifferensen, differensen som en procentandel av medianen i det inre, *och* Cliffs delta — en rangbaserad standardiserad effekt i [-1, 1] som avläses direkt från samma U-statistika (``δ = 2U/n₁n₂ − 1``). Detektion kräver både ett litet p **och** en effektstorlek över :data:`DEFAULT_MIN_EFFECT`, så att en signifikant men 0.4 % stor skillnad inte rapporteras som en kanteffekt.

records.context: **Evaporation is not a step function.** The profile walks inward ring by ring (outermost = ring 0), comparing each against the laboratory microplate core, so a gradient that reaches two microplate sample positions in is visible instead of being averaged into "the interior".
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Evaporation is not a step function.** The profile walks inward ring by ring (outermost = ring 0), comparing each against the plate core, so a gradient that reaches two wells in is visible instead of being averaged into "the interior".
records.translation: **Avdunstning är ingen stegfunktion.** Profilen går inåt ring för ring (yttersta = ring 0) och jämför var och en mot plattans kärna, så att en gradient som når två brunnar in syns i stället för att medelvärdesbildas in i "the interior".

records.context: **A gradient is not an edge effect.** An incubator or laboratory microplate-reader gradient runs *across* the laboratory microplate; evaporation runs *around* it. A linear column gradient leaves the outer ring with the same median as the interior (it collects both the high and the low end), so the ring test stays quiet while Spearman on the column index fires. Both are computed, both are reported, and :attr:`EdgeEffectReport.dominant` names which one better explains the laboratory microplate.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A gradient is not an edge effect.** An incubator or plate-reader gradient runs *across* the plate; evaporation runs *around* it. A linear column gradient leaves the outer ring with the same median as the interior (it collects both the high and the low end), so the ring test stays quiet while Spearman on the column index fires. Both are computed, both are reported, and :attr:`EdgeEffectReport.dominant` names which one better explains the plate.
records.translation: **En gradient är ingen kanteffekt.** En gradient från en inkubator eller plattläsare löper *över* plattan; avdunstning löper *runt* den. En linjär kolumngradient lämnar den yttre ringen med samma median som det inre (den samlar både den höga och den låga änden), så att ringtestet förblir tyst medan Spearman på kolumnindexet slår ut. Båda beräknas, båda rapporteras, och :attr:`EdgeEffectReport.dominant` anger vilken som bättre förklarar plattan.

records.context: The outer ring is compared against everything inside it with a two-sided Mann-Whitney U — rank-based, because per-microplate sample position aggregates of object measurements are skewed often enough that a t-test would be testing its own assumptions rather than the laboratory microplate. The accompanying Cliff's delta comes off the same U statistic, so effect size and p-value cannot disagree about which comparison was made.
records.label: spacr.plate_qc.detect_edge_effect#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The outer ring is compared against everything inside it with a two-sided Mann-Whitney U — rank-based, because per-well aggregates of object measurements are skewed often enough that a t-test would be testing its own assumptions rather than the plate. The accompanying Cliff's delta comes off the same U statistic, so effect size and p-value cannot disagree about which comparison was made.
records.translation: Den yttre ringen jämförs mot allt innanför den med ett tvåsidigt Mann-Whitney U — rangbaserat, eftersom aggregat per brunn av objektmätningar är skeva tillräckligt ofta för att ett t-test skulle testa sina egna antaganden snarare än plattan. Det tillhörande Cliffs delta beräknas från samma U-statistika, så att effektstorlek och p-värde inte kan vara oense om vilken jämförelse som gjordes.

records.context: Row and column gradients are tested separately with Spearman on the microplate sample position index. This is what keeps a laboratory microplate-reader or incubator gradient from being reported as an edge effect: a linear gradient across the laboratory microplate leaves the outer ring straddling both extremes, so its median matches the interior and the ring test correctly stays quiet.

records.source: Row and column gradients are tested separately with Spearman on the well index. records.translation: Rad- och kolumngradienter testas separat med Spearman på brunnsindexet. Det är detta som hindrar att en gradient från plattläsare eller inkubator rapporteras som en kanteffekt: en linjär gradient över plattan lämnar den yttre ringen spänd över båda ytterligheterna, så att dess median stämmer med det inre och ringtestet korrekt förblir tyst.

records.context: **Existing rows are removed prior to inserting replacements.** The measurement workflow calls ``to_sql(if_exists='append')`` to append rows. Measuring a field again would create a duplicate of each object rather than replace the old rows. This makes ``count_cell`` twice as large and biases the mean for each well. Removing old rows prior to another measurement makes the operation safe to repeat.
records.label: spacr.resume.clear_field_rows#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **This is the delete-before-insert.** Measure appends (``to_sql(if_exists='append')``), so re-running a field that already wrote rows adds a second copy of every object rather than replacing the first. Downstream, ``count_cell`` doubles, per-well means are computed over the doubled population, and nothing in the artifact says so. Calling this immediately before re-measuring a field is what makes a resume idempotent.
records.translation: **Detta är borttagningen före infogning.** Measure lägger till (``to_sql(if_exists='append')``), så att en omkörning av ett bildfält som redan har skrivit rader lägger till en andra kopia av varje objekt i stället för att ersätta den första. Längre fram fördubblas ``count_cell``, medelvärden per brunn beräknas över den fördubblade populationen, och inget i artefakten säger det. Att anropa detta omedelbart innan ett bildfält mäts om är det som gör en återupptagning idempotent.

records.context: **All or nothing.** Every table is deleted from inside one ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` … ``COMMIT``. If any statement fails — a missing table, a trigger, a lock — the transaction is rolled back and the database is left exactly as it was. A half-cleared field would be worse than an uncleared one.

If any statement fails — a missing table, a trigger, a lock — the transaction is rolled back and the database is left exactly as it was. A half-cleared field would be worse than an uncleared one.
records.translation: **Allt eller inget.** Varje tabell töms inifrån en enda ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` … ``COMMIT``. Om någon sats misslyckas — en saknad tabell, en trigger, ett lås — återställs transaktionen och databasen lämnas exakt som den var. Ett halvt rensat bildfält vore värre än ett orensat.

records.context: **Keyed on the field, not on its name.** The WHERE clause is equality over ``plateID``/``rowID``/``columnID``/``fieldID``, so clearing ``f1`` cannot touch ``f10``–``f19`` the way a ``LIKE 'plate1_A01_f1%'`` would. A table missing any of the four raises rather than running a broader delete.

A table missing any of the four raises rather than running a broader delete.
records.translation: **Nycklat på bildfältet, inte på dess namn.** WHERE-satsen är likhet över ``plateID``/``rowID``/``columnID``/``fieldID``, så att rensning av ``f1`` inte kan röra ``f10``–``f19`` på det sätt som en ``LIKE 'plate1_A01_f1%'`` skulle. En tabell som saknar någon av de fyra utlöser ett undantag i stället för att köra en bredare borttagning.

records.context: **Only measure's own tables.** Every table is checked against :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES` before anything is deleted, and one that is not on it aborts the whole call. ``measurements.db`` is shared — ``conversion_map``, ``align_coordinates`` and ``foreign_*`` live there and carry the same four identifier columns so that they join — and clearing a field out of those destroys the only record of how the project's files were named and registered.
records.label: spacr.resume.clear_field_rows#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Only measure's own tables.** Every table is checked against :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES` before anything is deleted, and one that is not on it aborts the whole call. ``measurements.db`` is shared — ``conversion_map``, ``align_coordinates`` and ``foreign_*`` live there and carry the same four key columns so that they join — and clearing a field out of those destroys the only record of how the project's files were named and registered.
records.translation: **Endast measures egna tabeller.** Varje tabell kontrolleras mot :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES` innan något tas bort, och en som inte finns på listan avbryter hela anropet. ``measurements.db`` delas — ``conversion_map``, ``align_coordinates`` och ``foreign_*`` finns där och bär samma fyra nyckelkolumner så att de kan sammanfogas — och att rensa ett bildfält ur dem förstör den enda registreringen av hur projektets filer namngavs och registrerades.

records.context: **Only rows measure itself wrote.** Owned by name is not owned in fact: in a project built by ``foreign.run_import`` the rows in ``cell`` are the import's, sitting under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table that is on the allow-list. Every DELETE is therefore narrowed by :func:`measure_rows_clause`, which is true only for rows holding a value in a column the importer never wrote. Clearing a field takes measure's rows for that field and leaves the import's — in the same table, in the same statement.
records.label: spacr.resume.clear_field_rows#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Only rows measure itself wrote.** Owned by name is not owned in fact: in a project built by ``foreign.run_import`` the rows in ``cell`` are the import's, sitting under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table that is on the allow-list. Every DELETE is therefore narrowed by :func:`measure_rows_clause`, which is true only for rows holding a value in a column the importer never wrote. Clearing a field takes measure's rows for that field and leaves the import's — in the same table, in the same statement.
records.translation: **Endast rader som measure själv skrev.** Ägd till namnet är inte ägd i praktiken: i ett projekt som byggts av ``foreign.run_import`` är raderna i ``cell`` importens, placerade under spaCR:s egna metadatakolumner i en tabell som finns på godkännandelistan. Varje DELETE begränsas därför av :func:`measure_rows_clause`, som är sann endast för rader som har ett värde i en kolumn som importören aldrig skrev. Att rensa ett bildfält tar measures rader för det bildfältet och lämnar importens kvar — i samma tabell, i samma sats.

records.context: "Already measured" deliberately means *present in every table this processing session writes*, not "present somewhere". ``_measure_crop_core`` inserts into ``cell``, then ``nucleus``, then ``pathogen``, then ``cytoplasm``, then ``png_list``, one call after another with a commit each — so a process killed between two of those calls leaves a field that has cell rows and no nucleus rows. Counting that field as done would permanently lose its nuclei; counting it as pending without clearing it first would duplicate its cells. It is reported through ``partial`` so the caller can do the third, correct thing: clear it and execute it again.
records.label: spacr.resume.completed_fields_in_db#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: "Already measured" deliberately means *present in every table this run writes*, not "present somewhere". ``_measure_crop_core`` inserts into ``cell``, then ``nucleus``, then ``pathogen``, then ``cytoplasm``, then ``png_list``, one call after another with a commit each — so a process killed between two of those calls leaves a field that has cell rows and no nucleus rows. Counting that field as done would permanently lose its nuclei; counting it as pending without clearing it first would duplicate its cells. It is reported through ``partial`` so the caller can do the third, correct thing: clear it and re-run it.
records.translation: "Already measured" betyder avsiktligt *finns i varje tabell som denna körning skriver*, inte "present somewhere". ``_measure_crop_core`` infogar i ``cell``, sedan ``nucleus``, sedan ``pathogen``, sedan ``cytoplasm``, sedan ``png_list``, ett anrop efter ett annat med en commit vardera — så att en process som dödas mellan två av dessa anrop lämnar ett bildfält som har cellrader och inga kärnrader. Att räkna det bildfältet som klart skulle permanent förlora dess kärnor; att räkna det som väntande utan att först rensa det skulle duplicera dess celler. Det rapporteras via ``partial`` så att anroparen kan göra det tredje, korrekta: rensa det och köra om det.

records.context: "Present" means present in a row **measure wrote**. Rows a foreign import copied into a canonical table do not count: a project built purely by import has ``cell`` as its only microscope field of view table and a row in it for every microscope field of view, so counting them would report the whole laboratory microplate as measured, ``measure_crop`` would execute nothing, and the imported numbers would stand as spaCR's output. A table holding nothing but imported rows is left out of the "every table this processing session writes" set entirely, so it cannot make every microscope field of view look partial either; it rejoins the moment measure puts a row in it. See :func:`measure_rows_clause`.
records.label: spacr.resume.completed_fields_in_db#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: "Present" means present in a row **measure wrote**. Rows a foreign import copied into a canonical table do not count: a project built purely by import has ``cell`` as its only field table and a row in it for every field, so counting them would report the whole plate as measured, ``measure_crop`` would run nothing, and the imported numbers would stand as spaCR's output. A table holding nothing but imported rows is left out of the "every table this run writes" set entirely, so it cannot make every field look partial either; it rejoins the moment measure puts a row in it. See :func:`measure_rows_clause`.
records.translation: "Present" betyder att det finns i en rad som **measure skrev**. Rader som en främmande import kopierade in i en kanonisk tabell räknas inte: ett projekt som byggts enbart genom import har ``cell`` som sin enda bildfältstabell och en rad i den för varje bildfält, så att räkna dem skulle rapportera hela plattan som uppmätt, ``measure_crop`` skulle inte köra något och de importerade talen skulle stå som spaCR:s utdata. En tabell som inte innehåller något annat än importerade rader lämnas helt utanför mängden "every table this run writes", så att den inte heller kan få varje bildfält att se partiellt ut; den kommer tillbaka i samma stund som measure lägger in en rad i den. Se :func:`measure_rows_clause`.

records.label: spacr.resume.plan_measure_resume#2

records.source: When resume *is* requested, in order:
records.translation: När återupptagning *begärs* sker följande, i ordning:

records.context: 1. Read the previous processing session's settings out of the ``settings`` table in ``measurements.db`` and throw :class:`ResumeRefused` if anything material differs. **This must happen before** ``spacr.io._save_settings_to_db`` overwrites that table with the current settings — hence the placement of the call in ``measure_crop``. 2. Enumerate the fields in ``merged/`` and *validate* each one: a truncated ``.npy`` from a crash mid-``np.save`` is pending, not done, and is counted as rejected. 3. Ask the database which fields already have rows in **every** table the processing session writes. Fields with rows in only some tables are partial — a process killed between two inserts — and are re-queued. 4. Delete every row belonging to a pending field before it is executed again. This is what stops the resume from doubling rows. 5. Print the plan.
records.label: spacr.resume.plan_measure_resume#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. Read the previous run's settings out of the ``settings`` table in ``measurements.db`` and raise :class:`ResumeRefused` if anything material differs. **This must happen before** ``spacr.io._save_settings_to_db`` overwrites that table with the current settings — hence the placement of the call in ``measure_crop``. 2. Enumerate the fields in ``merged/`` and *validate* each one: a truncated ``.npy`` from a crash mid-``np.save`` is pending, not done, and is counted as rejected. 3. Ask the database which fields already have rows in **every** table the run writes. Fields with rows in only some tables are partial — a process killed between two inserts — and are re-queued. 4. Delete every row belonging to a pending field before it is re-run. This is what stops the resume from doubling rows. 5. Print the plan.
records.translation: 1. Läs den föregående körningens inställningar ur tabellen ``settings`` i ``measurements.db`` och utlös :class:`ResumeRefused` om något väsentligt skiljer sig. **Detta måste ske innan** ``spacr.io._save_settings_to_db`` skriver över den tabellen med de aktuella inställningarna — därav anropets placering i ``measure_crop``. 2. Räkna upp bildfälten i ``merged/`` och *validera* vart och ett: en trunkerad ``.npy`` från en krasch mitt i ``np.save`` är väntande, inte klar, och räknas som avvisad. 3. Fråga databasen vilka bildfält som redan har rader i **varje** tabell som körningen skriver. Bildfält med rader i endast vissa tabeller är partiella — en process som dödades mellan två infogningar — och köas om. 4. Ta bort varje rad som tillhör ett väntande bildfält innan det körs om. Det är detta som hindrar återupptagningen från att fördubbla rader. 5. Skriv ut planen.

records.context: The rank is defined here, once, so both sides of a diff are ranked the same way: rows are sorted by **descending absolute score**, ties broken by structured-data name. Absolute, because a screening experiment's strongest hit is its largest effect in either direction and ranking a strong protective hit below a weak sensitising one would report rank churn that is an artefact of the sort. When no score column can be found the file's own row order is kept and :attr:`HitList.score_column` is empty, so a caller can tell a real ranking from a preserved one.
records.label: spacr.run_compare.read_hits#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The rank is defined here, once, so both sides of a diff are ranked the same way: rows are sorted by **descending absolute score**, ties broken by key. Absolute, because a screen's strongest hit is its largest effect in either direction and ranking a strong protective hit below a weak sensitising one would report rank churn that is an artefact of the sort. When no score column can be found the file's own row order is kept and :attr:`HitList.score_column` is empty, so a caller can tell a real ranking from a preserved one.
records.translation: Rangen definieras här, en gång, så att båda sidorna av en skillnad rangordnas på samma sätt: raderna sorteras efter **fallande absolut poäng**, med oavgjorda fall avgjorda efter nyckel. Absolut, eftersom en screens starkaste träff är dess största effekt i någon riktning, och att rangordna en stark skyddande träff under en svag sensibiliserande skulle rapportera en omflyttning i rang som är en artefakt av sorteringen. När ingen poängkolumn kan hittas behålls filens egen radordning och :attr:`HitList.score_column` är tom, så att en anropare kan skilja en verklig rangordning från en bevarad.

records.context: **The object type is part of that identity.** Object tables are one type per table, so without the type a nucleus labelled 1 and a pathogen labelled 1 in the same microscope field of view compose to the *identical* structured-data name. records.context: Two rules keep the change from breaking anything already written:
records.label: spacr.selection#16
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two rules keep the change from breaking anything already written:
records.translation: Två regler hindrar ändringen från att förstöra något som redan har skrivits:

records.context: *Untyped keys do not move.* The untyped form is byte for byte what it was, so every key in every stored selection, exported ``.h5ad`` and prediction bundle still composes and parses as it did. There is nothing on disk to migrate.
records.label: spacr.selection#17
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *Untyped keys do not move.* The untyped form is byte for byte what it was, so every key in every stored selection, exported ``.h5ad`` and prediction bundle still composes and parses as it did. There is nothing on disk to migrate.
records.translation: *Otypade nycklar flyttas inte.* Den otypade formen är byte för byte vad den var, så att varje nyckel i varje lagrat urval, exporterad ``.h5ad`` och prediktionspaket fortfarande sätts samman och tolkas som tidigare. Det finns inget på disk att migrera.

records.context: *An untyped structured-data name is less specific, not wrong.* ``plate1_r1_c1_f1_7`` means "the object labelled 7 in that microscope field of view", which is exactly what it always meant — so it matches that object whatever its type, rather than silently matching one of them. Symmetrically a typed structured-data name still matches a row that has not said what it is. :meth:`Selection.mask_for` and :meth:`ObjectRequest.select_from` both apply that rule, and it is the whole migration: an old structured-data name is read as the thing it always said, never re-read as something narrower.
records.label: spacr.selection#18
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: *An untyped key is LESS SPECIFIC, not wrong.* ``plate1_r1_c1_f1_7`` means "the object labelled 7 in that field", which is exactly what it always meant — so it matches that object whatever its type, rather than silently matching one of them. Symmetrically a typed key still matches a row that has not said what it is. :meth:`Selection.mask_for` and :meth:`ObjectRequest.select_from` both apply that rule, and it is the whole migration: an old key is read as the thing it always said, never re-read as something narrower.
records.translation: *En otypad nyckel är LESS SPECIFIC, inte fel.* ``plate1_r1_c1_f1_7`` betyder "the object labelled 7 in that field", vilket är exakt vad den alltid har betytt — så den matchar det objektet oavsett dess typ, i stället för att tyst matcha ett av dem. Symmetriskt matchar en typad nyckel fortfarande en rad som inte har angett vad den är. :meth:`Selection.mask_for` och :meth:`ObjectRequest.select_from` tillämpar båda den regeln, och den är hela migreringen: en gammal nyckel läses som det den alltid sade, och läses aldrig om som något snävare.
